title: StIA is a Novel Nucleoid-Associated Protein of Streptococcus pneumoniae that Activates DNA Topoisomerase I
authors: Antonio A. de Vasconcelos Junior; Pablo Herrera; Adela G. de la Campa; Mónica Amblar
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肺炎链球菌核仁相关蛋白StIA与dsDNA的非序列特异性结合及其对拓扑异构酶I的激活机制，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作体系，但非TF-DNA转录结合，且方法以实验为主、结构建模为辅，AI/物理模拟深度有限。
abstract: Topoisomerases are essential enzymes that maintain DNA topology. The activity of some of these enzymes is regulated by protein cofactors. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized nucleoid-associated protein from the human pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae that binds double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) in a sequence-independent manner both in vitro and in vivo and activates topoisomerase I (Topo I). This protein was named StIA (Streptococcal Topoisomerase I Activator). In vivo analyses showed that deletion of stIA impairs bacterial growth in the presence of the Topo I inhibitor seconeolitsine, whereas its overproduction decreases susceptibility to this compound. Consistent with these observations, StIA specifically stimulates Topo I activity without affecting DNA gyrase. StIA forms oligomers and assembles into higher-order nucleoprotein complexes upon DNA-binding. Mechanistic analyses revealed that StIA does not alter DNA cleavage by Topo I but specifically enhances the DNA religation step of its catalytic cycle. This activation is likely mediated through a direct protein-protein interaction, as StIA and Topo I physically associate in vitro . Structural modeling further supports the formation of a StIA-Topo I complex and identifies putative contact residues involved in the interaction. Collectively, these findings establish StIA as a novel nucleoid-associated with a dual function: promoting nucleoprotein complex assembly and stimulating Topo I activity through direct interaction with the enzyme. More broadly, our results suggest that the regulation of topoisomerase activity by accessory proteins may represent an important mechanism for fine-tuning DNA topological homeostasis and could provide new opportunities for the development of antibacterial therapies.
abstract_zh: 拓扑异构酶是维持DNA拓扑结构的关键酶。其中一些酶的活性受蛋白质辅因子的调控。在此，我们鉴定出一种来自人类病原体肺炎链球菌的、此前未被表征的核仁相关蛋白，该蛋白在体外和体内均以序列非依赖方式结合双链DNA（dsDNA），并激活拓扑异构酶I（Topo I）。该蛋白被命名为StIA（链球菌拓扑异构酶I激活因子）。体内分析表明，在存在Topo I抑制剂seconeolitsine的情况下，stIA的缺失会损害细菌生长，而其过表达则降低对该化合物的敏感性。与这些观察结果一致，StIA特异性刺激Topo I活性，而不影响DNA旋转酶。StIA形成寡聚体，并在结合DNA后组装成高阶核蛋白复合物。机制分析揭示，StIA不改变Topo I的DNA切割，而是特异性增强其催化循环中的DNA再连接步骤。这种激活可能通过直接的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用介导，因为StIA和Topo I在体外物理上相互关联。结构建模进一步支持StIA-Topo I复合物的形成，并识别出参与相互作用的推定接触残基。总体而言，这些发现将StIA确立为一种具有双重功能的新型核仁相关蛋白：促进核蛋白复合物组装，并通过与酶的直接相互作用刺激Topo I活性。更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，辅助蛋白对拓扑异构酶活性的调控可能代表一种微调DNA拓扑稳态的重要机制，并可能为抗菌疗法的开发提供新机遇。
